no_subagents/None.name: memory_search
no_subagents/None.description: Search the memory folder: fiches (what is known) and conversations (what was said, whole). Returns the path, the summary and an excerpt of each match — an excerpt is not the fiche: open it with memory_open before stating anything from it.

requete.description: Words to look for (a name, a subject, a phrase)

termes.description: Associated terms you choose — synonyms, the things the subject calls to mind (« fête des mères » → roses, bouquet, fleuriste). Each is searched too and the results are merged.

no_subagents/None.name: memory_open
no_subagents/None.description: Open a file of the memory folder, whole or a passage. A fiche comes back with the claims it holds you must announce as deduced (`a_annoncer`). Always open the fiche before answering what you know, and open the conversation behind a claim when asked where it comes from.

chemin.description: Path from memory_search or memory_write_fiche, as given

debut.description: Optional: first line of the passage (1 = first line)

fin.description: Optional: last line of the passage

no_subagents/None.name: memory_write_fiche
no_subagents/None.description: Write or rewrite a fiche: durable knowledge about a person, a story, a habit, a place. The title is a TRUE SENTENCE (« Françoise n'aime pas les roses »), not a label. Folders are yours to choose, few and shallow. Every claim carries its provenance and its source. `dit` = the owner said it (source: the conversation, with the minute; also needs `citation`: the owner's words, copied from his message at that minute); `observé` = seen in the app's data (source: `app : <la donnée>`; a habit the night read over a period, `app : …, sur la période du A au B`, is announced as deduced from an observation, like `déduit`); `déduit` = you inferred it (always announced as such when used). To correct a fiche that exists, open it, then rewrite it with `chemin`: send every claim that stays true in `affirmations`, and move what stopped being true to `remplacees` with the reason — it is dated and kept, never erased. Never write as `dit` or `observé` what you added yourself. The owner's conversation is already on file whole: this is for what is worth knowing again later.

titre.description: A true sentence, e.g. « Françoise n'aime pas les roses »

dossiers.description: Folders, outermost first, at most 3 (new fiche only)

chemin.description: Path of the fiche to rewrite (from memory_search)

resume.description: A few words on what the fiche is about

affirmations.description: Everything the fiche says as true now

source.description: Conversation or fiche path it comes from, or `app : <la donnée>`

heure.description: Conversation source: message minute `AAAA-MM-JJ HHhMM`, as in the file

citation.description: `dit`: the owner's words, copied as written (not stored)

valide_jusqu_au.description: Only when it has an end (« jusqu'au 20 », « cette semaine »): the last day it stays true, `AAAA-MM-JJ`. Left out on a rewrite, the day already written stays; empty removes it.

remplacees.description: Claims of the existing fiche that are no longer true

motif.description: What replaced it, or why it stopped

evoque.description: Situations or themes in which this fiche should come back

no_subagents/None.name: memory_log_miss
no_subagents/None.description: Call it when the owner tells you that you should have remembered something (« tu aurais dû t'en souvenir », « je te l'avais dit », « tu ne te rappelles pas ? ») — without waiting for a command. It keeps the miss as a case that is replayed every night against the memory, the cause is looked for and fixed, and it is reported. First find the fiche with memory_search (or write it with memory_write_fiche if it never existed, and describe it in `souvenir`), then log: `demande` = the words the owner said when it should have come back (the sentence where you missed it, not the reproach), `chemin` = the fiche that should have come back. Then answer « Vous avez raison, pardon. … je le retiens. » — do not mention the night or any follow-up.

demande.description: What the owner said when the fiche should have come back, as he said it

chemin.description: Path of the fiche that should have come back (from memory_search), if it exists

souvenir.description: What should have come back, in a few words (needed when there is no `chemin`)

no_subagents/None.name: add_instruction
no_subagents/None.description: Store a standing directive: a rule from the owner that lasts beyond this reply. Two kinds, and the kind decides who reads it: 'planning' (a moment that comes back, hours not to disturb him) is read by her daily planning, which schedules the runs; 'behavior' (tone, register, length) is injected into every reply. 'planning' is for when MAGGIE acts on her own; something the owner does that comes back is a task (create_task with rrule), not a directive. A way to carry out a kind of request is a skill (create_skill), a fact about him or the people around him a fiche (memory_write_fiche), one run at a set time schedule_proaction. A request for this reply only needs no directive. Before: list_instructions; a directive that says the same is not added twice.

content.description: The directive, in the user's own words

kind.description: 'planning' for a scheduling/notification rule, 'behavior' for a preference about tone, style or length

no_subagents/None.name: list_instructions
no_subagents/None.description: List the owner's standing directives (planning, behavior) with their ids. Read it before add_instruction, and to find the id delete_instruction needs.

kind.description: Only directives of this kind; omit for all of them

no_subagents/None.name: delete_instruction
no_subagents/None.description: Delete a standing directive by its id (from list_instructions). It cancels no run already scheduled (cancel_proaction) and no skill (delete_skill).

instruction_id.description: The ID of the instruction to delete

no_subagents/None.name: add_bilan_consigne
no_subagents/None.description: Evening review, Consignes step only: record ONE consigne the owner dictated, in one call. kind 'reminder' = something he must be told at a set time tomorrow (needs scheduled_at); 'task' = something he has to do tomorrow without a time (needs due_date), something to buy included, never a grocery item; 'instruction' = a rule that lasts or comes back. The tool creates the reminder, the task or the directive with the provenance 'bilan-soir' and writes it into the review's status: one call per consigne; during the review it replaces schedule_proaction, create_task, add_instruction and save_bilan_step for a consigne.

text.description: The consigne in the user's words, short ('Appeler le garage', 'Acheter du pain')

scheduled_at.description: reminder only: tomorrow, ISO 8601 with offset, e.g. 2030-11-15T09:00:00+01:00

instruction_kind.description: instruction only: 'planning' (default) for a date rule, 'behavior' for tone

no_subagents/None.name: create_skill
no_subagents/None.description: Create a skill: a procedure Maggie follows for a kind of request (when asked X, do Y), in markdown, listed by name and description in the prompt and loaded with get_skill. A general rule about how she should act is a skill, even about reminders or notifications. Tone and wording are a 'behavior' directive (add_instruction), when she acts on her own a 'planning' one, one run at a set time schedule_proaction, knowledge about the owner or the people around him a fiche (memory_write_fiche). Before: list_skills; a skill that already covers it is changed with update_skill, never doubled. The owner sees and edits skills in the admin, Réglages › Agent › Compétences. Tag the moment it applies, from what he said: 'moment:chat' (when he asks something), 'moment:proaction' (when a reminder or a proaction comes due), 'moment:planification' (the daily planning). A skill tagged with a moment is put in full in the prompt at that moment; one without stays in the index only.

description.description: Short description of what the skill does

tags.description: Keywords describing the skill, plus the moment it applies (e.g. ['rappel', 'notification', 'moment:proaction'])

content.description: The full skill procedure in markdown

no_subagents/None.name: list_skills
no_subagents/None.description: List the skills (name, description, tags). Read it before create_skill: a skill that already covers the request is updated, not created again.

no_subagents/None.name: get_skill
no_subagents/None.description: Charge une compétence de l'index « Compétences disponibles ». Quand sa description couvre la demande, charge-la au premier round, en même temps que tes premières lectures, et suis-la avant d'écrire.

no_subagents/None.name: update_skill
no_subagents/None.description: Change a skill that exists (name from list_skills); read it with get_skill first, since content replaces the whole text. Tags replace the old ones: keep them, and add or fix the moment the skill applies ('moment:chat', 'moment:proaction', 'moment:planification') when the user says when it should be applied.

tags.description: New tags, moment tags included (optional; they replace the old ones)

no_subagents/None.name: delete_skill
no_subagents/None.description: Delete a skill by name (from list_skills). A directive goes with delete_instruction, a scheduled run with cancel_proaction.

no_subagents/None.name: date_time
no_subagents/None.description: Exact date and time calculations — USE IT instead of computing in your head whenever a timezone, a daylight saving change, a weekday or a duration is involved. Never write an offset yourself. Actions: 'now' (current time in a place), 'convert' (an instant from one place to another), 'add' (instant + duration, negative to go back), 'diff' (time between two instants), 'weekday' (day of the week of a date). Places ('timezone', 'to_timezone', 'end_timezone') are a city, a region, a country or an IANA name ('Fort-de-France', 'New York', 'Europe/Paris'); omit them for the user's own timezone. A 'datetime' without offset is read as local time in 'timezone'; omit it for the current instant. Every result carries an 'iso' value with its offset, ready to pass as 'scheduled_at' to schedule_proaction or to build an event. This tool only computes: it schedules nothing, so a reminder still needs a tool call: create_task with a dueDate when the user has something to do (« rappelle-moi d'aller faire X »), schedule_proaction when Maggie herself must act or speak at that time. Calendar units (years, months, weeks, days) keep the wall-clock time across a clock change; clock units (hours, minutes, seconds) are real elapsed time.

datetime.description: ISO 8601 date or datetime, e.g. 2026-03-28 or 2026-03-28T15:00. Default: now.

timezone.description: Place of 'datetime' (source place for convert). Default: the user's timezone.

no_subagents/None.name: get_coach_method
no_subagents/None.description: Lit la méthode du coach sportif, une section à la fois. section : principes · semaine · echelles · progression · seance · degradees · calibrage · sources. Sans section : la table des sections.

no_subagents/None.name: answer_approval
no_subagents/None.description: Approve or deny an action held for the user's validation (its approvalId is given with the message the user is answering), exactly as the « Autoriser » / « Refuser » buttons do. Only for an approval the user is answering in this message — never decide one on your own: any other call is refused.

approval_id.description: The approvalId of the message being answered

no_subagents/None.name: ask_owner
no_subagents/None.description: Ask the owner a short question with options to tick, and stop there: his answer comes back as his next message. Use it for any hesitation that fits options — what he expects from his request (« je dois penser à prendre… » : a task with the list, planned, or just a note?), which of two plausible readings, whether to go ahead with something irreversible — never to ask a free-text question and never for a clear request. 'text' is one natural sentence without Markdown; 'options' are 2 to 6 short labels; 'multiple' is true when several can be ticked together.

no_subagents/None.name: send_voice_message
no_subagents/None.description: Send the user a voice message: the text is spoken in their chosen voice, recorded, and lands in the thread as an audio message they can play now or later. Use it when the user asks for a vocal (« envoie-moi un vocal… ») or a directive asks for one (a morning digest « en vocal »). Write the text for the ear: plain sentences, no Markdown, no list, no table, no URL. The message is in the thread once the tool answers: reply nothing else.

text.description: What Maggie says, written to be heard

screen.description: The screen the vocal belongs on, when a skill says so (the digest skill: "digest"); its notification then opens that screen instead of the thread. Omit it otherwise.

no_subagents/None.description: Events

no_subagents/None.description: Recipes

subagents/proaction.name: memory_search
subagents/proaction.description: Search the memory folder: fiches (what is known) and conversations (what was said, whole). Returns the path, the summary and an excerpt of each match — an excerpt is not the fiche: open it with memory_open before stating anything from it.

requete.description: Words to look for (a name, a subject, a phrase)

termes.description: Associated terms you choose — synonyms, the things the subject calls to mind (« fête des mères » → roses, bouquet, fleuriste). Each is searched too and the results are merged.

subagents/proaction.name: memory_open
subagents/proaction.description: Open a file of the memory folder, whole or a passage. A fiche comes back with the claims it holds you must announce as deduced (`a_annoncer`). Always open the fiche before answering what you know, and open the conversation behind a claim when asked where it comes from.

chemin.description: Path from memory_search or memory_write_fiche, as given

debut.description: Optional: first line of the passage (1 = first line)

fin.description: Optional: last line of the passage

subagents/proaction.name: memory_write_fiche
subagents/proaction.description: Write or rewrite a fiche: durable knowledge about a person, a story, a habit, a place. The title is a TRUE SENTENCE (« Françoise n'aime pas les roses »), not a label. Folders are yours to choose, few and shallow. Every claim carries its provenance and its source. `dit` = the owner said it (source: the conversation, with the minute; also needs `citation`: the owner's words, copied from his message at that minute); `observé` = seen in the app's data (source: `app : <la donnée>`; a habit the night read over a period, `app : …, sur la période du A au B`, is announced as deduced from an observation, like `déduit`); `déduit` = you inferred it (always announced as such when used). To correct a fiche that exists, open it, then rewrite it with `chemin`: send every claim that stays true in `affirmations`, and move what stopped being true to `remplacees` with the reason — it is dated and kept, never erased. Never write as `dit` or `observé` what you added yourself. The owner's conversation is already on file whole: this is for what is worth knowing again later.

titre.description: A true sentence, e.g. « Françoise n'aime pas les roses »

dossiers.description: Folders, outermost first, at most 3 (new fiche only)

chemin.description: Path of the fiche to rewrite (from memory_search)

resume.description: A few words on what the fiche is about

affirmations.description: Everything the fiche says as true now

source.description: Conversation or fiche path it comes from, or `app : <la donnée>`

heure.description: Conversation source: message minute `AAAA-MM-JJ HHhMM`, as in the file

citation.description: `dit`: the owner's words, copied as written (not stored)

valide_jusqu_au.description: Only when it has an end (« jusqu'au 20 », « cette semaine »): the last day it stays true, `AAAA-MM-JJ`. Left out on a rewrite, the day already written stays; empty removes it.

remplacees.description: Claims of the existing fiche that are no longer true

motif.description: What replaced it, or why it stopped

evoque.description: Situations or themes in which this fiche should come back
